story: First Infocom Z-machine implemented in hardware
text: Many Infocom employees are present in the documentary Get Lamp: [VIDEO] Recommended if text games are of interest to you.
If you like text adventure games, check out Jason Scott's documentary GET LAMP about the history of text adventure games, including interviews with some Infocom developers: [VIDEO] [LINK]

story: Iconoclast: a Gothic/Cyberpunk MUD RPG, Online Since 1996
text: Oh the MUDs! Props to Forest’s edge and TempusMUD. Text is the ultimate medium because it directly connects with our imagination. I remember jumping out of my chair after reading a line of text on my screen. Recommend watching “Get lamp” documentary to fans of MUDs, text adventures and those born after: [VIDEO]
He also did a documentary about text adventure games called "GET LAMP" which I enjoyed a lot: [VIDEO]
Jason Scott (of textfiles.com) made a great documentary video about the Adeventure game. I picked up a copy at DEFCON about 15 years ago. [LINK] [VIDEO]
You can watch the non-interactive version of the documentary with some commentary by its maker in this Google Tech Talk: [VIDEO]

Related: there's a few versions of "get lamp" documentary online ( [VIDEO] ) or you can get the movie directly from getlamp.com. These histories (the maher link above, the getlamp doc, etc) bring back a lot of great memories. EDIT: the youtube link above looks like it's actually the getlamp movie being shown at a google event, with an audience (audience sounds in there now and then).

He also gave us the brilliant BBS: The Documentary [LINK] GET LAMP: The Text Adventure Documentary (shot in 1080p) [VIDEO] and (apart from his many talks) his podcast "Jason Scott talks his way out of it" which is just gem after gem of documented tech ephemera. [LINK] It's baffingly hard to quantify how many people he (and all the other great people at the Internet Archive) has affected with his bullheaded conservation efforts.
